narrative:
The model determined that you have a 63% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is well above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the amount you requested, and the length of the loan. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the rejection. Among approved applicants only 12.6% have a negative balance, while the majority (59%) have no checking account or a positive one. This situation pushed the prediction strongly toward bad credit risk.

The loan amount you asked for (1,659 DM) actually worked in your favor. Approved applicants request an average of 3,020 DM, so your smaller request helped pull the prediction back toward approval. Unfortunately this positive effect was not large enough to overcome the other factors.

The 24-month duration you requested also increased the risk score. Approved loans average only 19 months, so the longer repayment period added further weight toward denial.

Taken together, the negative checking-account status outweighed the helpful smaller loan size and created too high an overall risk for the bank to approve the application.

You should focus on improving your checking-account balance and, when you reapply, consider requesting a shorter loan term. These two changes would remove the largest obstacles the model identified and greatly improve your chances of approval.
